readerTitle: Every law firm says it's client-focused. How does one stand out?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (물류 고객을 둔 법률사무소, 부품 제조사의 사내 법무팀) · 모든 인물과 회사, 수치는 설명용
insight: 포지셔닝은 '우리가 더 낫다'를 외치기 전에 '누구와 비교될지'부터 고르는 일이다. 비교 대상을 고른 뒤 그 안에서 증명할 수 있는 차이로 이긴다.
misconception: 고객을 넓게 잡을수록 기회가 많아진다. 경험, 신뢰, 빠른 응대 같은 장점을 많이 나열할수록 돋보인다.

sources.text: Keller, K. L., Sternthal, B., & Tybout, A. (2002). Three Questions You Need to Ask About Your Brand. Harvard Business Review.
Ries, A., & Trout, J. (1981). Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind. McGraw-Hill.
모든 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: Marlow & Reyes, 부품 제조사 법무팀, 변호사 12명, 법무팀 4명 등은 모두 가상 설정입니다. 실제 법률사무소 이름과 겹치지 않는지 게시 전에 확인하세요.
7번 카드의 '많은 지역에서 변호사의 광고 문구(예: specialist 표기)를 규제한다'는 일반적 서술입니다. 특정 국가의 규정은 다루지 않았습니다. 표현이 과하지 않은지 확인하세요.
레슨 안의 개념 정의(frame of reference, points of difference)가 STR-05-02, STR-05-03 본문의 정의와 같은 표현인지 맞춰 보세요.

cards.title: Every law firm says it's client-focused. How does one stand out?
body: Open the websites of three business law firms in any city. You'll likely read the same words: *experienced*, *client-focused*, *full-service*, *trusted*.
If every firm makes the same promise, the promise tells a client nothing. Today you'll position one small firm using two tools from this unit.

image.label: Three nearly identical law firm websites side by side
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 노트북 화면 세 개가 나란히 놓여 있고 각 화면에 거의 같은 문구 "Experienced. Client-focused. Full-service."가 적혀 있음. 기둥 사진과 저울 아이콘도 셋 다 같음. 실제 법률사무소 이름이나 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Pick the firm's headline.
body: Marlow & Reyes is a 12-lawyer firm in a port city. About half its work comes from trucking companies, warehouses and freight forwarders: contracts, cargo damage claims and customs disputes.
The partners want one line for the website and pitch decks. Which do you choose?

options.text: A full-service business law firm for companies of every size
options.feedback: It welcomes everyone, but it sets the **frame of reference** as 'business law firms'. There, a 12-lawyer firm loses to downtown firms with ten times the people.

options.text: Lawyers for companies that move goods
options.feedback: This sets a **frame of reference** where the firm's real strength counts. Clients now compare it with generalists who need freight law explained to them.

options.text: The friendliest business law firm in the region
options.feedback: It tries for a **point of difference**, but inside a frame where the firm is small. And 'friendly' is easy for any rival to claim.

cards.title: The frame picks your rivals.
body: A warehouse owner facing a damaged-cargo claim doesn't compare every lawyer in the city. She compares the options that seem to fit her problem.
Call Marlow & Reyes a 'full-service firm' and it lands next to big firms. It loses on size, reach and brand every time.
Call it 'lawyers for companies that move goods' and the comparison flips. Now the big firms are the outsiders, and **the small firm is the expert**.

cards.title: Frame of reference
body: From STR-05-02: the **frame of reference** is the group of options customers use to judge you. It tells them *what you are* before you tell them why you're better.
You can't win every comparison. So choose a frame where your strengths matter most and your weaknesses matter least.

image.label: Same small firm shown in a big frame and a narrow frame
image.brief: 두 개의 액자 비교. 왼쪽 큰 액자 "Business law firms" 안에서 작은 사무소 건물이 큰 빌딩들 사이에 묻혀 있음. 오른쪽 작은 액자 "Law for companies that move goods" 안에서는 같은 건물이 가운데에서 크게 보이고 옆에 트럭과 컨테이너 아이콘. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.softwareNote: A small analytics tool that calls itself 'a business intelligence platform' gets compared with giant software suites. 'Sales reports for online shop owners' picks rivals it can actually beat.

cards.title: Now win inside the frame.
body: The new headline is live. Other firms in the city also take freight cases, so clients still compare a few options.
Which message should Marlow & Reyes put right under the headline?

options.text: Responsive, experienced and trusted by our clients
options.feedback: Every rival says this, so it isn't a **point of difference**. It's the minimum a client expects from any firm.

options.text: Fixed fees for standard cargo claims, handled by lawyers who worked in logistics
options.feedback: A strong **point of difference**: clients want price certainty, the firm can prove it, and generalist rivals can't easily say the same.

options.text: The lowest hourly rates in the city
options.feedback: It is different, but any firm can cut its rates tomorrow. It also attracts clients who will leave for the next cheaper offer.

cards.title: Points of difference
body: From STR-05-03: a **point of difference** is something customers value, that you can prove, and that rivals in your frame can't easily claim.

Run each message through those three tests. 'Responsive' fails the third. 'Lowest rates' passes today and fails next month. Fixed fees plus real logistics experience passes all three, at least until rivals catch up.

image.label: Three filters testing each message
image.brief: 깔때기 세 개가 위에서 아래로 이어진 인포그래픽. 각각 "Customers want it", "You can prove it", "Rivals can't easily claim it". 위에서 메시지 카드 여러 장이 들어가고 맨 아래에는 "Fixed fees + logistics experience" 한 장만 통과.

cards.title: A narrow position is a promise.
body: The frame only works if the firm has real depth. If two of twelve lawyers know freight law, clients will notice by the second meeting.
Narrowing also costs something. Some partners' clients won't fit the headline. But a position is what you **lead with**, not a list of clients you refuse.
Also check local rules. In many places, rules limit what law firms may say in ads, such as calling themselves specialists.

cards.title: Now it's a legal team inside a company.
body: You lead a four-person legal team at a parts manufacturer. Sales reps call legal 'where deals go to wait', so they sign side agreements without you.
You want them to come to you early. What do you lead with?

options.text: An email listing every service the legal team offers
options.feedback: It explains more, but the team stays in the same **frame of reference**: the department that slows deals down.

options.text: Present the team as 'the fastest way to get a deal signed', with standard contracts approved within one business day
options.feedback: This sets a new **frame of reference** (deal helpers, not gatekeepers) and backs it with a **point of difference** sales reps can test.

options.text: Rename the team 'Legal Partners' and add a friendly intro video
options.feedback: A friendlier image may help, but without a change sales can feel, it's a new label on the same experience.

cards.title: Choose your comparison, then win it.
body: Tools used today: **frame of reference** (STR-05-02) to pick who you're compared with, and **points of difference** (STR-05-03) to win inside that frame.
**Try it today:** finish the line 'We are the ___ for ___'. Then write one thing you offer that rivals in that frame can't truthfully say.
